newsitem.title: USA: Gelbard to coordinate U.S.'s Bosnia policy.
newsitem.headline: Gelbard to coordinate U.S.'s Bosnia policy.

text.p: Robert Gelbard, who helped lead the U.S. battle with Colombia over drugs, will be the new U.S. coordinator for Bosnia policy, U.S. officials said on Thursday.

Secretary of State Madeleine Albright is expected to formally announce Gelbard's appointment at a noon EDT (1600 GMT) news briefing before he leaves with a team of other officials for 10 days of travel, mostly in the Balkans, they said.
Gelbard, a career diplomat, has been assistant secretary of state for international narcotics matters.

In that capacity, he was instrumental in confronting Colombian President Ernesto Samper with charges that he took drug money for his election campaign and in deciding to de-certify Colombia as a country that cooperates with the United States in the fight against narcotics trafficking.
Gelbard will take over the Bosnia portfolio from Assistant Secretary of State for European and Canadian Affairs John Kornblum.
Administration sources have said since January that Kornblum would be the next U.S. ambassador to Germany although that and other appointments have yet to be formally announced by the White House.
